days.note_headline: Record operating cash is masking slower collections, and rising rates will expose it
days.note_opening: Headline cash strength across Treasury and Finance is hiding a deterioration in collections. Hackett's survey of the 1,000 largest North American companies shows operating cash flow at 17% of revenue, a 13-year high, whi

items.headline: Centalion and Komgo cut trade-finance issuance time 55% with an AI agent
items.summary: Centalion Group and Komgo deployed an AI Treasury agent that answers natural-language queries on trade-finance facility capacity, enforces controls through an orchestration layer and keeps human approval at every step. Issuance time fell 55%, amendments 80%, freeing 60+ working days yearly.

items.headline: Prolific Banking's FI-Streams portal cuts bank API rollout to under four months
items.summary: On 9 November 2026 Prolific Banking launched the FI-Streams Developer Portal and APIs, letting banks offer branded self-service APIs to corporates in under four months rather than 12–18 months. Payments, reporting and webhooks are covered, shortening Treasury's wait for connectivity.

items.headline: Hackett finds receivables up 11%, twice revenue growth, as DSO slips again
items.summary: Hackett's 2026 survey of the 1,000 largest North American companies put operating cash flow at 17% of revenue, a 13-year high. Receivables rose 11%, twice revenue growth, DSO worsened 2.1 days for a third year, and the cash-conversion cycle improved only 0.2 days.

items.headline: Only 38% of CFOs see better customer payment behaviour, down from 73%
items.summary: 52% of CFOs now prioritise clearer cash-flow views, yet only 38% report improved customer payment behaviour, down from 73% a year earlier. Supply-chain programme settlement volumes rose 35% year-on-year, suggesting vendor-payment deferral is reaching its limits as a working-capital lever.

items.headline: Canada's Real-Time Rail goes live with 8 participants and 24/7 settlement
items.summary: Payments Canada launched Real-Time Rail on 9 November 2026, offering 24/7 interbank clearing and settlement on ISO 20022 with immediate funds availability. 8 institutions, including Bank of America and Wealthsimple, joined at launch; a Canada-EU RTR link is under discussion but not yet operational.

items.headline: OCC Bulletin 2026-54 maps AI risk to 16 components across six pillars
items.summary: OCC Bulletin 2026-54 sets out an AI supervisory framework of 16 components across six pillars: purpose, risk, control, oversight, resilience and assurance. It creates no new enforceable standards but applies existing risk-management concepts, signalling examiners will evaluate material AI use.

items.headline: Bank of England lifts Bank Rate to 4.00%, first rise since August 2023
items.summary: The Bank of England raised Bank Rate to 4.00% in November 2026, its first increase since August 2023, with markets pricing up to three more hikes. Sterling treasurers face December hike risk, while euro treasurers may see a December adjustment before eventual ECB easing.

items.headline: EY finds corporate stablecoin use doubled to 18% in live production
items.summary: EY's July–August 2026 survey found 18% of corporates running stablecoins live in production, double the 9% of 2025. Only 5% of financial institutions have no plans to offer stablecoin services, with cross-border supplier payments and B2B acceptance leading use cases.

items.headline: U.S. Q3 GDP grows 3.4%, reinforcing the Fed's higher-for-longer stance
items.summary: U.S. GDP expanded at a 3.4% seasonally adjusted annualised rate in Q3, driven by resilient domestic spending and strong capital investment. Firm employment data support the Fed's higher-for-longer stance into the final months of 2026, leaving little near-term rate relief for dollar borrowers.

items.headline: FATF finds only 34% of jurisdictions largely compliant on virtual assets
items.summary: On 5 November 2026 the Financial Action Task Force published its seventh targeted update, finding only 34% of jurisdictions largely compliant with virtual asset AML/CFT standards. Gaps in Travel Rule operationalisation and enforcement affect corporate payments routed through digital asset channels.

items.headline: IASB keeps IFRS 16 intact but tightens lease cash outflow disclosures
items.summary: Concluding its post-implementation review on 28-29 October 2026, the IASB found IFRS 16 working as intended. It will strengthen disclosure of total cash outflows for lease payments and how they are classified across operating, investing and financing activities, sharpening cash-flow reporting.

days.note_headline: The SEC wants proof behind Finance AI claims, and spreadsheets still run cash
days.note_opening: AI claims across Treasury and Finance now need evidence that matches daily practice. The SEC set up a Financial Reporting and Accounting Unit in August 2026, and Enforcement Director David Woodcock said on 30 October 202

items.headline: Atlar deploys Claude-powered agents for OnePay's scheduled Treasury workflows
items.summary: On 12 November 2026, Atlar put Claude-powered autonomous agents to work in OnePay's Treasury operations, running scheduled cash position analysis and bank fee audits with approval controls. Agents connect to all OnePay banks and its ERP, showing how sign-off gates keep autonomy accountable.

items.headline: Huntington and Kyriba launch Intelligent Treasury for multi-bank cash visibility
items.summary: Huntington announced Intelligent Treasury, built with Kyriba, as of 5 November 2026. It offers consolidated balances and transactions, daily-to-monthly cash forecasting, centralised payment workflows and ERP integration across multiple banking relationships, giving treasurers one view of cash across their banks.

items.headline: Finmo board finds 80–90% of Asia cash positioning still runs on Excel
items.summary: Finmo's advisory board found 80–90% of Asia cash-position work runs on Excel fed by portals, emails, ERPs and Treasury systems. Multi-entity consolidation is hardest, as accounting platforms are single-entity by design and lag 1–2 weeks in transaction coding.

items.headline: Citigroup urges treasurers to classify jurisdictions to free trapped cash
items.summary: Citigroup's liquidity guidance asks treasurers to sort jurisdictions as liberal, semi-restrictive or restrictive. The aim is better cash visibility, mobilising trapped cash and building market-based concentration frameworks, giving groups a structured basis for deciding where liquidity can realistically be pooled.

items.headline: BIS says G20 end-2027 cross-border instant-payment goal is unachievable
items.summary: Instant-payment rails on ISO 20022 still diverge on message versions, field requirements and address formats, forcing translation between them. The BIS December 2025 assessment confirms the G20 end-2027 cross-border goal is unachievable despite policy completion, so cross-border friction will outlast the deadline.

items.headline: SEC to test whether AI use matches public disclosures in 2027 exams
items.summary: A new SEC Financial Reporting Unit will assess whether AI use aligns with public disclosures, focusing on fair representation, operational consistency and whether algorithm recommendations match investor profiles. Heightened 2027 examination priorities put AI governance squarely on the CFO office's agenda.

items.headline: KPMG tells CFOs AI governance is a lifecycle cost, not a launch cost
items.summary: KPMG argues strong AI governance speeds enterprise adoption, but generic AI-leader claims need verifiable support that stays consistent across earnings releases, calls and filings. The CFO office must build those controls upfront rather than retrofit them, budgeting governance across the whole lifecycle.

items.headline: CME interest-rate derivatives hit record 14.8 million contracts a day in October
items.summary: CME Group said on 3 November 2026 that October 2026 interest-rate derivative average daily volume reached 14.8 million contracts, up 28% year-over-year, with U.S. Treasury futures up 48%. Corporates and asset managers are hedging diverging central bank rate paths and persistent energy-driven inflation.

items.headline: Zanders and Standard Chartered say tokenisation beats 2–3 day correspondent settlement
items.summary: Joint analysis from Zanders and Standard Chartered finds that tokenising cash, deposits, securities and collateral as programmable blockchain tokens enables near-real-time settlement, against 2–3 day correspondent-banking cycles. That cuts reconciliation effort and frees trapped liquidity.

items.headline: Markets price 87% chance of December Fed hike after hot October CPI
items.summary: Headline CPI of 0.4% and core CPI of 0.3%, both above consensus, on 10 November pushed markets to price an 87% probability of a 25 basis-point hike on December 9, up from 72% a week earlier. Governor Christopher Waller backed a quarter-point rise.

items.headline: Euro slides to 18-month low at 1.1095 as rate gap widens
items.summary: EUR/USD hit 1.1095, an 18-month low, as 10-year US Treasury yields stood above 5% on 11 November 2026 after the hot October CPI print, while ECB hike odds stayed lower. The wider US-eurozone rate differential raises the stakes for euro-dollar hedging.

items.headline: FinCEN cuts MEXC Global from US system over $16 billion in flows
items.summary: On 6 November 2026, FinCEN ordered covered financial institutions to stop moving funds to or from Seychelles-based crypto exchange MEXC Global, citing $16 billion in sanctions-linked flows tied to Russian illicit Finance and cybercrime. The order, effective 10 December 2026, tests onboarding and counterparty screening.

items.headline: SEC Enforcement to scrutinise whether corporate AI disclosures match reality
items.summary: On 30 October 2026, SEC Enforcement Director David Woodcock said the Division will test whether AI disclosures represent capabilities and material risks. A Financial Reporting and Accounting Unit from August 2026 pursues accounting fraud, auditing misconduct; 2027 priorities cover AI claims and audit committee oversight.

days.note_headline: Costlier hedging and slower customer payments make working-capital resilience the Finance priority
days.note_opening: Working capital is becoming harder and dearer to defend across Treasury and Finance. Only 38% of CFOs polled by PYMNTS report better customer payment behaviour, against 73% a year earlier. Sikich found 48% of 183 Finance

items.headline: Trovata deploys autonomous Treasury agents on Amazon Bedrock and AgentCore
items.summary: Trovata has put autonomous agents to work in Treasury operations on Amazon's Bedrock and AgentCore platforms, covering cash forecasting, variance analysis and anomaly detection without extra development work. The question for treasurers is who reviews agent decisions before they shape cash positions.

items.headline: Kyriba Open APIs connect live Treasury data to 1,000+ banks and ERPs
items.summary: Kyriba's Open APIs feed live Treasury data and financial workflows straight into enterprise applications, with a Developer Portal offering 1,000+ bank integrations, ERP and partner links, a full API catalogue and an App Marketplace. More connections mean more access rights for treasurers to govern.

items.headline: Only 38% of CFOs see better customer payment behaviour, down from 73%
items.summary: A PYMNTS survey finds just 38% of CFOs report improved customer payment behaviour, against 73% a year earlier, as procurement teams use extended terms as a competitive tool. Treasurers are moving from optimising cash towards building working-capital resilience against volatility.

items.headline: Rate volatility and working capital each worry 48% of Finance leaders
items.summary: Sikich surveyed 183 Finance leaders in August–September 2026: 48% named interest-rate volatility and 48% named working-capital optimisation as top Treasury concerns, while 42% worried about access to capital. The results frame 2027 funding plans around rate risk and liquidity.

items.headline: FedNow adds ISO 20022 cross-border capability and payee name verification
items.summary: The FedNow Service has launched an ISO 20022 message format capability and a payee name verification API to support cross-border pilot operations. It lays groundwork for instant payments across jurisdictions, and name checks give treasurers an extra control against misdirected funds.

items.headline: IAASB publishes first quality management guide for AI-enabled audit tools
items.summary: The IAASB has released its first quality management guidance for AI-enabled tools in audit and assurance engagements, answering global calls for consistency as firms apply AI to high-stakes financial judgements. For controllers, it sets the bar audit firms must meet when AI touches their numbers.

items.headline: RBI's 20% cash reserve on FX derivatives makes Indian dollar hedging dearer
items.summary: India's RBI introduced a foreign-exchange risk reserve (FERR) on 10 October 2026, requiring banks to hold a 20% cash reserve against eligible FX derivative contracts. One-year forward premia reached 4.85% by mid-October before easing to 3.91%, making dollar hedging dearer for treasurers.

items.headline: Banque de France outlines private clearing for tokenised deposits via Pontes
items.summary: Banque de France First Deputy Governor Denis Beau set out a hypothetical private-sector clearing mechanism for tokenised bank deposits that would settle through the Pontes wholesale service. The aim is to keep central-bank money central in Europe as dollar stablecoins grow.

items.headline: All 71 economists expect ECB to lift deposit rate to 2.75% in December
items.summary: All 71 economists Reuters polled on November 10–12 expected the ECB to raise its deposit rate to 2.75% in December; over one-third see another hike in Q1 2027. With eurozone inflation at 4%, treasurers must plan for diverging euro and dollar rate paths.

items.headline: OFAC extends Cuba sanctions to electronics, manufacturing, marine and technology sectors
items.summary: On 4 November 2026, OFAC expanded Executive Order 14404 authority to Cuba's electronics, manufacturing, marine and technology sectors, allowing designation of foreign persons active there. Coverage already spanned energy, defence, metals, mining, financial services and security, so counterparty screening scope must widen.

items.headline: SEC Enforcement to test AI disclosure accuracy in 2027 examinations
items.summary: On 30 October 2026, SEC Enforcement Director Woodcock signalled closer scrutiny of whether firms' AI use matches Form ADV disclosures and marketing materials. Examinations in 2027 will test the accuracy of claims, operations against disclosures and whether algorithms advise in line with investor profiles.

days.note_headline: Dollar strength and hike bets now reward Finance Teams that hedge fast with controls
days.note_opening: Hedging speed has become a control capability for Treasury and Finance. Two-year yields jumped 34 basis points in the week to 4.87% as December Fed hike odds reached 86-90%. JPMorgan shows agents queuing hedges for a 9-s

items.headline: JPMorgan whitepaper shows Treasury agents hedging FX within a 9-second approval loop
items.summary: JPMorgan's June 2026 whitepaper shows autonomous Treasury AI spotting FX mismatches, sourcing hedge proposals from three counterparty quotes via API and queuing them for human approval. A 9-second approval workflow with audit trails models delegation inside policy limits rather than escalation.

items.headline: API-first TMS designs swap overnight batch files for live intraday bank feeds
items.summary: Modern Treasury Management Systems now connect to banks through APIs first, normalising real-time balances and transactions across entities and currencies into live aggregated positions. Continuous refresh lets Treasury make intraday liquidity decisions without waiting for overnight batch files to land.

items.headline: Hackett puts North American working capital opportunity at record $1.94 trillion
items.summary: Hackett Group's 5 October 2026 survey of North America's 1,000 largest companies found the working capital opportunity rose 12% to $1.94 trillion. Receivables jumped 29% to $773 billion as DSO worsened for a third year, with receivables growth of 11% outpacing 6% revenue growth.

items.headline: SWIFT delays November 2026 structured-address mandate, revised timing due December
items.summary: SWIFT has postponed the planned November 2026 switch-off of unstructured addresses after readiness gaps surfaced across the industry in August 2026. Banks and central banks are consulting on new timing before December 2026 guidance, and unstructured-address payments will still eventually be rejected.

items.headline: EY tells CFOs to wrap agents around TMS and ERP, not replace them
items.summary: EY's agentic AI playbook for CFOs sets four design principles: overlay agents on TMS and ERP via APIs, keep agents advisory with human approval, stand up a governance council and audit logging before scaling, and track cycle-time reduction, not accuracy alone.

items.headline: Crown Agents Bank goes live on interest-rate swaps within four months
items.summary: Crown Agents Bank moved from vendor selection to live interest-rate hedging within four months, using the ALMIS Cobalt TMS with embedded hedge-accounting controls. The bank can now manage interest-rate risk in a structured way for the first time, with accounting controls built in.

items.headline: Visa adds Monad to its stablecoin settlement programme
items.summary: On 10 November, Visa added Monad as a settlement option for participating issuers and acquirers. The blockchain offers stablecoin settlement with sub-second finality and private settlement that shields commercially sensitive details while keeping full audit and regulator access intact.

items.headline: Dollar hits 19-month high as December Fed hike odds reach 86-90%
items.summary: On 13 November, EUR/USD fell to 1.1052, its lowest since April 2025, as December Fed hike odds of 86-90% lifted Treasury yields; two-year yields rose 34 basis points in the week to 4.87%. The dollar index hit a 19-month high near 103.20.

items.headline: EU extends chemical weapons sanctions regime to 2031, listings reviewed annually
items.summary: On 12 October 2026, the EU Council extended its chemical weapons sanctions framework to 30 October 2031, with individual listings under annual review until 30 October 2027. Nine non-EU countries will align, according to the High Representative, widening the screening footprint.

items.headline: SEC 2027 exam priorities test whether AI use matches company disclosures
items.summary: On 9 November, the SEC Division of Examinations set 2027 priorities that test whether AI used in core operations, from investment analysis and fraud detection to back-office work, matches what public companies tell investors, with tighter oversight of AI-driven compliance and trading.

days.note_headline: Trapped cash is now the top Finance priority, and reporting rules are following
days.note_opening: Liquidity visibility has become the organising problem for Treasury and Finance. Citi Institute finds 72 per cent of global corporates now rank freeing trapped supply-chain liquidity as their leading priority, up from 66

items.headline: Ripple's GSmart agents now span five Treasury workflow domains
items.summary: Ripple has extended its GSmart agentic platform across five domains: forecasting, liquidity, risk, reconciliation and reporting. Each agent runs on a schedule or trigger within policy limits set in Knowledge Studio, and treasurers set autonomy per workflow, making delegation a documented control choice.

items.headline: REST APIs and lakehouses bring real-time TMS data to Treasury
items.summary: Treasury integrations involving ING, Datalog and Databricks now rely on RESTful APIs to expose cash flows, balances and FX exposures in real time from TMS platforms such as Kyriba and Datalog. Near-real-time lakehouse pipelines feed AI and reporting, so data lineage becomes a control issue.

items.headline: 72 per cent of corporates now rank trapped liquidity as top priority, says Citi
items.summary: The Citi Institute Supply Chain Financing Report finds 72 per cent of global corporates rank freeing trapped liquidity as their leading priority for the next 12 months, up from 66 per cent. For 64 per cent, simply measuring supply-chain liquidity is the driver.

items.headline: China opens cross-border cash pooling to multinationals nationwide
items.summary: China is rolling out cross-border cash pooling nationwide, letting multinational groups concentrate onshore and offshore subsidiary cash in one virtual account. Fewer bilateral FX transactions and simpler group-level liquidity deployment could ease trapped-cash constraints for Treasury teams.

items.headline: SWIFT postpones SR2026, pushing cross-border payment changes to 2027 or later
items.summary: SWIFT has postponed Standards Release 2026 (SR2026), originally due 14 November. A partial SR2026 covering all MT messages and most ISO 20022 categories is planned for June 2027, while MT Category 1, CBPR+ and SCORE+ changes move to Standards Release 2027 or later.

items.headline: OCC framework grades bank super intelligence use across 16 components and six pillars
items.summary: OCC Bulletin 2026-54, issued on 10 November 2026, sets how examiners will assess banks' use of super intelligence. Its 16 components sit in six pillars, from Purpose to Assurance, and risk tiers depend on consequences and transfer of agency, not technical sophistication.

sources.name: Office of the Comptroller of the Currency

items.headline: State Street sees geopolitical and tariff risks lifting FX volatility into 2027
items.summary: State Street expects FX risk to stay elevated as political uncertainty in major economies shapes tariff policy and Fed policy diverges from other central banks. Trump administration policies could reshape 2027 FX volatility and, with it, corporate currency exposure.

items.headline: Tokenised deposits suit internal pooling; stablecoins lead on cross-border flows
items.summary: EY survey and The Paypers analysis find tokenised deposits efficient for instant internal sweeping and intercompany settlement within one banking ecosystem. Stablecoins keep an edge as neutral bridges for multi-bank and cross-border flows, with 67 per cent of corporate respondents prioritising lower transaction costs.

items.headline: US two-year yield hits 4.88% as December Fed hike odds reach 88%
items.summary: Two-year Treasury yields reached 4.88% on 16 November 2026, with the biggest weekly jump in over two years. Markets price 88% odds of a December hike; the 10-year rose to 5.15% on 16 November 2026 and the dollar index hit 103.40.

items.headline: All 71 Reuters economists expect ECB to lift deposit rate to 2.75%
items.summary: All 71 economists polled by Reuters on 12 November 2026 expect a 25-basis-point ECB rise to 2.75% in December, with eurozone inflation at a three-year high of 4.0%. Most see this as the peak, but over one-third expect another hike in early 2027.

items.headline: FinCEN cuts MEXC Global off from US system over $16.7 billion Russia flows
items.summary: FinCEN on 10 November 2026 named MEXC Global a primary money laundering concern tied to Russian illicit Finance, barring all US transmittals involving the exchange from 10 December 2026. It cites $16.7 billion in flows from May 2021 to May 2026 and AML/CFT non-compliance.

items.headline: IASB moves to tighten IFRS 16 lease cash outflow disclosures
items.summary: In October 2026 the IASB tentatively decided to amend IFRS 16 so lessees disclose total lease payment cash outflows separately and split amounts across operating, investing and financing activities. Treasury and controllers gain clearer sight of lease-driven liquidity calls.

days.note_headline: Regulators are now grading AI autonomy, so Finance must prove every delegated decision
days.note_opening: Supervisors and auditors are building the rulebook for AI that acts, not just advises. The OCC now grades bank AI across 16 components in six pillars, weighing reversibility, autonomy and customer impact. On 10 November

items.headline: Deutsche Bank and Ant Digital map agentic AI across liquidity and trade Finance
items.summary: Deutsche Bank and Ant Digital Technologies published a whitepaper setting out agentic AI use cases in Treasury liquidity management, cross-border payment orchestration and trade finance. It stresses institutional controls over delegated decisions, the point treasurers must settle before any agent touches cash.

items.headline: Treasury agents move from generating insights to taking action within set limits
items.summary: Treasury AI is moving beyond dashboards to agents that execute tasks inside human-defined boundaries. Key deployments now run parts of the daily cash cycle, from monitoring and categorisation to reconciliation and forecasting, under treasurer-set rules and approval limits, making those limits the core control.

items.headline: JPMorgan expands SAP API links to cut manual Treasury file handling
items.summary: JPMorgan has extended the API infrastructure linking its payments solutions directly into SAP ERP environments. Companies can view balances, transactions and payment tracking inside existing systems without manual file handling, shrinking the manual touchpoints Treasury must control.

items.headline: JPMorgan says unmatched payer data leaves receivables cash trapped
items.summary: JPMorgan warns that accounts receivable teams unable to match payer identity to invoice detail leave working capital stuck. Enhanced AR platforms now connect receivables data with payment records to release that stranded cash, a direct lever on cash conversion for Treasury and Finance.

items.headline: Half of SWIFT payments reach the recipient bank within 40 seconds
items.summary: SWIFT data shows half of payments on its network arrive at the recipient bank within 40 seconds and 75% within 10 minutes, meeting its one-hour end-to-end target. Country-level processing still varies significantly, so treasurers cannot assume uniform speed across corridors.

items.headline: PCAOB and SEC officials press for AI governance and process-level risk assessment
items.summary: PCAOB and SEC officials said AI, especially 'super intelligence', needs clear governance plans, effective risk assessment at process level and internal controls that reflect its opacity and probabilistic behaviour. Finance Teams deploying AI in close or Treasury processes can expect auditors to test that.

items.headline: OCC grades bank AI across 16 components in six risk pillars
items.summary: The OCC issued AI supervision guidance sorting bank AI use into 16 components across six pillars. Risk is classified by consequence, weighing reversibility, customer impact, autonomy and data sensitivity, a useful template for Treasury and Finance Teams assessing agents that move cash.

items.headline: RBI imposes 20% cash reserve on corporate FX hedges above USD 2 million
items.summary: On 10 October 2026 the RBI required authorised dealers to hold a 20% cash deposit with the central bank on corporate hedging FX derivatives above USD 2 million notional. Rupee protection against currency weakness becomes substantially dearer for Treasury teams.

items.headline: DBS and Kinexys launch 24/7 tokenised dollar transfers between US and Singapore
items.summary: On 16 November 2026, DBS Token Services and Kinexys by JPMorgan began instant US dollar transfers on a 24/7 basis between tokenised deposit accounts, with Partior's shared ledger orchestrating settlement. Ant International is the first institutional client, pointing to round-the-clock US-Singapore liquidity for treasurers.

items.headline: Dollar index hits 19-month high as EUR/USD slips to 1.1007
items.summary: On 16 November the dollar index reached 103.50, a 19-month high last seen in April 2025, after stronger inflation data and hawkish Fed signals of a likely December hike. EUR/USD fell to 1.1007, sharpening hedging decisions for euro exposures.

items.headline: EU sanctions 113 Russian targets across banks, energy and shadow fleet
items.summary: On 16 November 2026 the EU Council hit 113 targets, 12 individuals and 101 entities, with asset freezes and travel bans. They include nearly 50 Russian banks, energy firms, Wildberries and Ozon shareholders and shadow-fleet intermediaries in the UAE and China, plus Seychelles and Oman.

items.headline: OFAC designates 10 targets in Iranian defence electronics procurement networks
items.summary: On 29 September 2026 OFAC designated 10 individuals and entities, including Iran-based Kavoshcom and Hong Kong-based EC Mojo Technology, for procuring military electronics for Iran's Ministry of Defence, Aerospace Industries Organization and ballistic missile programmes. Electronics supplier checks now need sharper screening.

items.headline: PCAOB creates 'Super Intelligence Unit' to police AI misconduct in audits
items.summary: On 10 November 2026 the PCAOB announced five new specialised enforcement units, including a 'Super Intelligence Unit' to investigate emerging risks and possible misconduct from AI use in public company audits. Controllers should expect auditors to scrutinise AI-generated evidence more closely.

items.headline: IASB explores separate disclosure of IFRS 16 lease cash outflows
items.summary: In October 2026 the IASB decided to explore requiring IFRS 16 lessees to disclose components of total lease cash outflows separately and show which cash flow statement line items hold each. Treasury and reporting teams may need finer-grained lease cash data.

days.note_headline: Autonomous execution has reached corporate Treasury, making guardrails a Finance-wide design job
days.note_opening: Agentic AI is executing, not just advising, in Treasury. Google runs a three-agent system across $100bn of fixed income, $50bn of FX hedging and $20bn of operating cash in 60 countries, while Microsoft's six-agent MICS a

items.headline: Deutsche Bank and Ant Digital chart autonomous AI for liquidity and FX
items.summary: Deutsche Bank and Ant Digital published a roadmap for agentic AI that forecasts liquidity shortfalls, weighs response options and executes compliant actions across fund transfers, investments, financing and FX. For treasurers, it is a blueprint for where autonomous approvals will need policy limits.

items.headline: Google runs $100bn portfolio through three-agent cash-management system
items.summary: Google disclosed a three-agent system covering forecasting, evaluation and execution that manages $100bn of fixed income, $50bn of FX hedging and $20bn of operating cash across 60 countries. It freed staff for higher-value work and lifted incremental interest income.

items.headline: Microsoft's six-agent MICS system moves Treasury to touchless-first execution
items.summary: Microsoft deployed six AI agents in its MICS system, handling email, cash and remittances, shifting Treasury from assisted work to human-led autonomous execution. Defined guardrails govern fund disbursements and payment matching, the control boundary every Finance Team will need to specify.

items.headline: Northern Data picks Embat's API-first TMS to centralise 100+ bank accounts
items.summary: Northern Data selected Embat's cloud-native, API-first TMS to centralise 100+ global bank accounts and integrate with SAP S/4HANA. It swaps years-long legacy deployments for rapid consolidation, a faster route to group cash visibility.

items.headline: Over 40% of treasurers want 24/7 money-market fund liquidity, AFP finds
items.summary: The AFP 2026 survey found more than 40% of treasurers expect money-market funds to offer 24/7 liquidity, as real-time payments and instant settlement blur available and invested cash. Rising demand for weekend cash deployment pressures investment policies and fund providers alike.

items.headline: Bacardi extends DPO by 25 days through structured working-capital framework
items.summary: Bacardi cut DSO by one day, reduced non-aged days inventory outstanding by 15 days and extended days payable outstanding (DPO) by 25 days in fiscal 2025. Data-driven working-capital management lifted ROIC, showing how much cash sits in operating discipline.

items.headline: SWIFT delays SR2026 payments changes, deferring ISO 20022 structured-address mandate
items.summary: SWIFT postponed the November 2026 structured-address mandate for ISO 20022 cross-border payments, deferring all SR2026 payments changes with no firm new date and citing industry unreadiness. An update on its consultation with banks, central banks and corporates is due by December.

items.headline: Finance Teams speed agentic AI adoption, but 27% flag compliance risk
items.summary: A Zapier survey shows Finance Teams ramping up agentic AI, yet 27% cite regulatory compliance and data-privacy concerns as barriers and 24% flag accuracy and reliability risks in autonomous execution. Control design, not appetite, is now the constraint.

items.headline: Foreign investors' FX hedge ratios fell to 44.5% in October
items.summary: Foreign investors' FX hedge ratios declined to 44.5% in October 2026 as US interest-rate changes and the technology stock rally shifted sentiment, leaving significant unhedged exposure to US equities and fixed income despite concentration risks. Useful context for treasurers setting hedge policy.

items.headline: KeyCorp adds $6.8bn forward-starting swaps, taking its position to $10.1bn
items.summary: KeyCorp added $6.8bn of receive-fixed forward-starting interest-rate swaps in Q3 2026, after $3.3bn in Q2, lifting its total position to $10.1bn. The bank is locking in attractive rates to protect future interest income, a template for rate-sensitive balance sheets.

items.headline: HKMA and SWIFT deepen work on tokenised-deposit cross-border payments
items.summary: The Hong Kong Monetary Authority and SWIFT have deepened collaboration to explore tokenised-deposit mechanisms for cross-border payments, building on Project Ensemble's CBDC interoperability work with Bank of China, Standard Chartered and HSBC Hong Kong. Cross-border settlement efficiency is the prize for treasurers.

items.headline: Technology firms step up FX hedging into 2027 on geopolitical and rate risk
items.summary: Technology companies increased FX hedging through November 2026 as geopolitical tensions, tariff risks and interest-rate shifts pushed currency-exposure management up corporate agendas heading into 2027. For treasurers, it sets a peer benchmark for 2027 hedging policy.

items.headline: FinCEN proposes beneficial-ownership verification for every new corporate account
items.summary: On 13 November 2026, FinCEN proposed that covered financial institutions identify and verify beneficial owners whenever a legal entity customer opens a new account, plus updated identifying-number standards and risk-based ongoing due diligence. Corporate onboarding timelines and counterparty screening are directly affected.

items.headline: IASB moves to require IFRS 16 lease cash outflow disclosure by classification
items.summary: On 28 October 2026 the IASB tentatively decided to amend IFRS 16 so lessees disclose total cash outflows for lease payments to lessors, split by operating, investing and financing classifications. Lease-related liquidity becomes clearer for treasurers and controllers alike.

sources.name: IFRS Foundation - Statement of Cash Flows and Related Matters Project Update

days.note_headline: Treasury AI now pays for itself, and auditors are setting the evidence bar
days.note_opening: AI in Treasury now delivers measurable returns, and audit oversight is moving as fast. Flex put $50 million of idle cash to work through Atlar AI agents, earning 5x ROI in year one. The PCAOB created a Super Intelligence

items.headline: Atlar AI agents put Flex's idle $50 million to work overnight
items.summary: Flex uses Atlar AI agents to move cash from operating funds into overnight liquidity funds each night, logging every transfer for treasurer review. The programme put $50 million of zero-yield balances to work and delivered 5x ROI in year one, with oversight intact.

items.headline: Google Treasury runs three AI agents across 60+ countries, piloting with HSBC
items.summary: Google Treasury has built a three-agent AI system that runs daily liquidity across 60+ countries, forecasting cash flows, collecting counterparty rates and recommending investments that managers approve. The HSBC pilot in India and Taiwan shows banks being drawn into agent workflows.

items.headline: Citi finds 72% of corporates rank trapped liquidity release first
items.summary: Citi research in October 2026 found 72% of global companies name releasing trapped liquidity as their top strategic priority for the next 12 months, up from 66% at the start of 2026. And 64% see supply-chain cash extraction as a key working-capital driver.

items.headline: HSBC launches HSBCnio, letting client AI tools reach account data via MCP
items.summary: HSBC rolled out HSBCnio in September 2026, linking banking services to corporate workflows through web, mobile and API channels. Its Model Context Protocol lets clients' AI tools access authorised account data under permission-based controls, making access rights a Treasury governance question.

items.headline: PCAOB sets up Super Intelligence Unit to police AI misconduct in audits
items.summary: On 11 November 2026 the PCAOB created a Super Intelligence Unit inside its enforcement division, focused on emerging risks and possible misconduct from AI use in audits. Finance Teams using AI in close and reporting face sharper auditor scrutiny.

items.headline: Fed minutes point to further hikes, with 95% odds priced for December
items.summary: October minutes published 18 November 2026 show almost all Fed participants expect further increases to return inflation to 2%. Markets price a 95% chance of a December hike. The median projection is 4.1% at end-2026 and 2027, keeping Treasury planning on higher for longer.

items.headline: HKMA and SWIFT test tokenised deposits for 24/7 cross-border payments
items.summary: The Hong Kong Monetary Authority says HSBC, Standard Chartered and Bank of China are testing SWIFT's blockchain ledger with Project Ensemble for tokenised-asset and tokenised-deposit settlement. The exploratory project targets 24/7 cross-border payments using bank account-based tokens, at stablecoin speed without private-issuer risk.

items.headline: Dollar index hits 19-month high of 103.87 as Fed eyes December hike
items.summary: The US dollar index rose to 103.87 on 18 November, a 19-month peak, and EUR/USD slipped to 1.0965 after hawkish Fed inflation remarks and strong US data. Nearly all Fed officials expect a quarter-point December increase, lifting Treasury yields and repricing euro exposures.

items.headline: EU sanctions 113 more Russian individuals and entities, including financial institutions
items.summary: On 16 November 2026 the EU Council added restrictive measures on 113 individuals and entities, among them financial institutions and energy companies, to curb Russia's war financing and shadow fleet support. Screening lists and counterparty checks need updating promptly.

items.headline: IAASB approves first quality management guide for AI-enabled audit tools
items.summary: On 28 October 2026 the IAASB approved the first in a series of guides applying audit quality standards to AI-enabled tools, with firm-level and engagement-level controls guidance due in early 2027. Controllers should expect tighter questions on AI-generated evidence.

days.note_headline: Money and agents now run around the clock, so Finance controls must too
days.note_opening: Treasury and Finance now operate on rails that never close, run by software agents. DBS and JPMorgan's Kinexys deployed instant 24/7 USD transfers between the United States and Singapore on 16 November 2026. Hyundai Card

items.headline: BNY and Microsoft agents negotiate a US Treasury bill trade within set limits
items.summary: On 18 November 2026, BNY Mellon and Microsoft used AI agents under defined governance controls to agree price terms on a US Treasury bill trade, with human traders approving before execution. Treasurers get a working template for autonomous negotiation with sign-off retained.

items.headline: Hyundai Card trials AI agents managing Euro liquidity on JPMorgan's Kinexys
items.summary: Hyundai Card completed a proof of concept with JPMorgan's Kinexys on 18 November 2026, in which AI agents managed Euro liquidity, compared FX quotes from multiple banks and executed cross-currency transfers. Digitally signed mandates and automated escalation controls show how delegation can be bounded.

items.headline: JPMorgan API v6.5.4 adds third-party app search for ERP and TMS links
items.summary: JPMorgan's Business Direct Connect API v6.5.4, released on 17 November 2026, adds third-party app search and website URI information fields. Wider programmatic access to Treasury and payments data should make ERP and TMS integrations easier to build.

items.headline: HSBCnio adds MCP server access to live Treasury data for AI assistants
items.summary: HSBC's HSBCnio now offers Model Context Protocol server connectivity, letting AI assistants access live account balances, transactions, FX rates and payment status without code. Direct integration with Treasury management systems and AI workflows cuts the manual work of gathering bank data.

items.headline: Standard Chartered and Ant International pilot early liquidity for tokenised MMFs
items.summary: On 10 November 2026, Standard Chartered and Ant International completed a pilot redemption liquidity facility that lets corporates draw cash from tokenised money market fund holdings before the underlying fund settles. It closes a timing gap that can hold up Treasury liquidity.

items.headline: HSBC unveils HSBCnio, giving corporate AI tools read-only bank data access
items.summary: HSBC announced HSBCnio on 26 October 2026, combining transaction banking services with AI through APIs and Model Context Protocol. Corporate clients' own AI tools get secure, read-only access to authorised account and transaction data, a clear control boundary for automating Treasury workflows.

items.headline: PCAOB creates Super Intelligence Unit to investigate AI misconduct in audits
items.summary: The Public Company Accounting Oversight Board announced on 11 November 2026 a specialised Super Intelligence Unit within its Enforcement Division to probe risks and misconduct from AI use in public company audits, while building AI enforcement tools. Controllers should expect sharper questions.

items.headline: Apple and Micron add over 60% to FX derivative notionals in Q3
items.summary: In Q3 2026, technology firms including Apple and Micron each lifted FX derivatives notionals by over 60%, responding to persistent geopolitical uncertainty and rate volatility expected to last into 2027. Peers are extending protection, a useful benchmark for hedge policy reviews.

items.headline: StraitsX and OCBC pilot B2B stablecoin payments into ordinary bank accounts
items.summary: StraitsX and OCBC announced a pilot on 23 November 2026 letting businesses receive cross-border B2B stablecoin payments directly into existing OCBC accounts, without handling stablecoins themselves. Dedicated wallet addresses identify payments and support same-day settlement, easing reconciliation for receivables teams.

items.headline: DBS and Kinexys enable 24/7 USD tokenised deposit transfers between US and Singapore
items.summary: On 16 November 2026, DBS and JPMorgan's Kinexys deployed instant 24/7 USD transfers between blockchain-based accounts in the United States and Singapore. Institutional clients can move on-chain liquidity on demand outside banking hours, so cut-off times no longer cap cross-border funding.

items.headline: Dollar index hits 104.45 as markets price 94% chance of December hike
items.summary: The dollar index reached 104.45 on 23 November, a 19-month high, while EUR/USD touched a 19-month low near 1.0899. Markets price a 94% chance of a 25bp Fed hike in December, and Nvidia's CEO reinstatement added momentum, so euro exposures need attention.

items.headline: FinCEN proposes stricter beneficial owner checks at corporate account opening
items.summary: FinCEN proposed a rule on 17 November 2026 requiring financial institutions to identify beneficial owners of legal entity customers at account opening and re-verify when reliability is in doubt. It bars ITINs for beneficial owners and permits collecting immigration status, so expect heavier onboarding.

sources.name: U.S. Department of the Treasury FinCEN

items.headline: IAASB issues first of four guides on quality management for AI audit tools
items.summary: The International Auditing and Assurance Standards Board published on 12 November 2026 the first of four guides on quality management for AI-enabled audit tools. Supporting ISQM 1 and ISA 220, it tackles hallucinations, automation bias and human oversight, shaping what auditors ask Finance.

days.note_headline: AI now negotiates Treasury trades, and enforcement makes human sign-off non-negotiable
days.note_opening: AI agents now negotiate trades, yet enforcement is making human sign-off the control that matters. BNY and Microsoft let agents negotiate a US Treasury bill trade on 17 November 2026, with traders approving terms before

items.headline: BNY and Microsoft agents negotiate a US Treasury bill trade
items.summary: On 17 November 2026, BNY and Microsoft completed an industry-first pilot in which AI agents negotiated a US Treasury bill trade within predefined parameters. Human traders reviewed and approved the terms before execution through existing systems, a template for supervised agentic dealing.

items.headline: Embat uses JPMorgan's BAS API to connect bank accounts in seconds
items.summary: On 4 November 2026, Embat deployed JPMorgan's new Banking Authorization Service (BAS) API, letting corporate clients authenticate and link JPMorgan accounts to its platform in seconds without IT. Real-time data flows to ERP systems, cutting onboarding friction for Treasury.

items.headline: DBS and Kinexys enable 24/7 USD tokenised deposit transfers across US and Singapore
items.summary: On 16 November 2026, DBS and JPMorgan's Kinexys launched interoperability for instant USD transfers between blockchain-based institutional accounts in the US and Singapore, weekends included. Multinationals can deploy on-chain USD liquidity on demand 24/7, extending cash positioning beyond banking hours.

items.headline: HKMA and SWIFT explore tokenised deposits linked to Project Ensemble
items.summary: On 16 November 2026, the Hong Kong Monetary Authority deepened work with SWIFT on multi-currency tokenised deposits for cross-border transactions. Bank of China (Hong Kong), Standard Chartered and HSBC are helping connect the SWIFT ledger with Project Ensemble's settlement layer, shaping future payment routes.

items.headline: PCAOB launches Super Intelligence Unit to investigate AI misconduct in audits
items.summary: On 11 November 2026, the PCAOB created a Super Intelligence Unit in its Enforcement Division to investigate AI-related audit risks and misconduct without discouraging appropriate adoption. It will also build its own AI enforcement tools, so controllers should expect sharper scrutiny of AI-assisted work.

items.headline: US Treasury cleared repo reaches $7.9 trillion, sponsored share a record 30.9%
items.summary: On 24 November 2026, ISDA-Actrix reported cleared repo average daily volume of $7.9 trillion in October 2026, up 3.4% month-on-month. Sponsored client repo reached $2.5 trillion, a record 30.9% share, reflecting counterparty risk management and lower balance-sheet demand after the SEC Treasury clearing mandate.

sources.name: ISDA-Actrix US Treasury Repo Market Clearing Indicators

items.headline: HKMA extends Project Ensemble pilot to 24/7 tokenised deposit settlement
items.summary: On 2 November, the Hong Kong Monetary Authority widened Project Ensemble's pilot to support 24/7 settlement of tokenised deposit transactions in tokenised central bank money. With 12 banks and 20 industry partners, it lets real-value Treasury operations run outside traditional system hours.

items.headline: ECB sources see 25bp December hike as near-certain, then a pause
items.summary: On 29 October, ECB sources said a 25bp rise on 17 December is all but certain after recent energy-price increases. Policymakers expect to pause afterwards because sharp gains in market borrowing costs could weigh on growth, framing euro funding and hedging plans.

items.headline: Markets price 93% odds of a December Fed hike as dollar holds firm
items.summary: As of 25 November, prediction markets price a 93% chance of a 25bp Fed increase on 9 December. The dollar index sits near 103.85, close to a 19-month peak, after a 1.9% monthly gain, keeping pressure on dollar funding costs and FX hedging budgets.

items.headline: OFAC designates Iranian exchange houses in Operation Economic Outcast
items.summary: On 23 November 2026, OFAC designated over two dozen Iranian exchange houses, front companies and personnel to disrupt Iran's global shadow banking networks under Operation Economic Outcast. Treasury teams should expect refreshed screening lists and closer scrutiny of counterparties linked to sanctions evasion.

items.headline: OCC fines Bank of America record $750 million over BSA/AML failures
items.summary: On 11 November 2026, the OCC assessed Bank of America a record $750 million civil penalty for systematic transaction monitoring gaps, late suspicious activity reports covering billions of dollars, and thin BSA/AML staffing and training over years. Banking partners' compliance weaknesses can become corporate operational risk.

sources.name: Office of the Comptroller of the Currency

items.headline: IASB closes IFRS 16 review and plans targeted lease accounting fixes
items.summary: On 23 November 2026, the IASB completed its post-implementation review of IFRS 16 Leases, finding the standard works as intended. Targeted improvements will aim to make reporting more useful and cut lessee application costs without compromising information quality, welcome news for controllers.

days.note_headline: Dearer money makes cash visibility the Finance priority, from agent approvals to lease disclosures
days.note_opening: Cash visibility has become the Finance priority as money gets dearer. Markets price 97% odds of a 25bp Fed hike at the 8-9 December meeting, lifting the dollar to 19-month highs. AstraZeneca stretched its cash forecast f

items.headline: Stripe Treasury lets AI agents move corporate money via MCP server
items.summary: Stripe moved Treasury into public preview on 19 November 2026, letting AI agents transfer funds, convert currencies and pay vendors through its Model Context Protocol server. Approval workflows are configurable, and every money movement needs human sign-off by default, a ready-made control point.

items.headline: AstraZeneca stretches cash forecast from one week to five weeks
items.summary: AstraZeneca extended its cash-forecasting horizon from one week to five weeks by pulling payment and receivables data in near real-time from multiple SAP systems into a platform blending statistical methods and machine learning. Treasurers gain better liquidity planning and less spreadsheet dependency.

items.headline: ING's Stable Pricing Cash Pool lets treasurers fix pool rates for set windows
items.summary: Through Bank Mendes Gans, ING introduced a Stable Pricing Cash Pool that lets multinational treasurers fix interest rates for defined windows, such as one week, while keeping legal daily revocability. ING hedges the rate exposure, giving treasurers firmer sight of borrowing costs.

items.headline: Hackett finds €1.26 trillion trapped in European working capital
items.summary: The Hackett Group's analysis of Europe's 1,000 largest publicly traded nonfinancial companies found €1.26 trillion trapped in working capital. Their cash conversion cycle still improved 1.8 days (4%) in 2025, with days sales outstanding and days inventory outstanding both falling, yet sizeable cash remains locked.

items.headline: Canada's Real-Time Rail goes live with 24/7 ISO 20022 instant settlement
items.summary: Payments Canada launched the Real-Time Rail on 9 November 2026, offering instant settlement, 24/7 availability and data-rich ISO 20022 messaging. A joint Canada–EU commitment targets interlinking instant payment systems, which would ease cross-border transactions for Treasury teams paying between the two.

items.headline: SWIFT postpones SR2026 cross-border changes, keeping unstructured addresses alive
items.summary: SWIFT has deferred every SR2026 ISO 20022 cross-border payment change planned for November 2026, citing uneven industry readiness. Removal of unstructured postal addresses is on hold and they remain accepted, with a new timeline expected by December, giving Treasury teams breathing room on data remediation.

items.headline: Finance Teams flag 27% compliance-risk concern over agentic AI adoption
items.summary: An industry survey shows a 27% compliance-risk concern among Finance Teams as treasurers speed up agentic AI deployment. Findings stress SOX controls, audit logs and human-in-the-loop governance before autonomous execution, while CFO offices prioritise inventorying AI use cases and embedding AI-disclosure requirements in SOX walkthroughs.

items.headline: Markets price 97% odds of December Fed hike, dollar hits 19-month high
items.summary: On 25 November, investors priced a 97% probability of a 25-basis-point Fed rise in December 2026, driven by hawkish official commentary and stronger-than-expected inflation data. The dollar reached 19-month highs, and markets expect further tightening into 2027, a live issue for dollar exposures.

items.headline: HKMA launches CMU Digital Asset Platform with 24-hour tokenised settlement
items.summary: The Hong Kong Monetary Authority launched the CMU Digital Asset Platform on 25 November, supporting paperless debt securities issuance and 24-hour tokenised settlement across multiple currencies. Direct links to RTGS systems and CBDCs bring round-the-clock settlement closer to treasurers issuing or holding debt.

items.headline: Fed holds at 3.75%-4.00% but signals 25bp December hike
items.summary: Federal Reserve survey data released on 25 November confirmed elevated inflation and strong growth, with rates held at 3.75%-4.00% and further tightening signalled. Markets price 97% odds of a 25bp hike at the 8-9 December meeting, and two officials openly back a December increase.

items.headline: FinCEN proposes risk-based beneficial ownership checks at account opening
items.summary: FinCEN proposed amendments to customer due diligence rules on 17 November 2026, dropping the need to identify beneficial owners at every new account opening. Banks would verify on a risk basis at opening, when facts question reliability, or during ongoing reviews, potentially easing corporate onboarding.

items.headline: IASB closes IFRS 16 review, eyes clearer lease cash-flow disclosures
items.summary: The IASB published its IFRS 16 feedback statement on 23 November 2026 and will explore requiring lessees to disclose the components of total lease-related cash outflows and where they sit in the cash flow statement, targeting inconsistent application that clouds cash comparisons.

items.headline: IASB opens IFRS 9 hedge accounting review, feedback due 26 January 2027
items.summary: On 16 November 2026 the IASB launched its post-implementation review of IFRS 9 and IFRS 7 hedge accounting requirements. Stakeholders have until 26 January 2027 to comment on costs, usefulness and application challenges, including diversity in practice, a chance for treasurers to shape hedge rules.
